newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel decides against outlawing subway cult.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel decides against outlawing subway cult.

text.p: Japan's Public Security Commission on Friday decided not to invoke a draconian 1952 subversion law to outlaw the religious sect accused of the deadly nerve gas attack on Tokyo subways, officials said.

The independent commission's widely anticipated decision not to apply the Antisubversive Activities Law to Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) rejects a request filed last July by the Justice Ministry's Public Security Investigation Agency.
The six-member commission unanimously rejected the request, ruling that the doomsday cult no longer posed a threat to Japanese society, the officials said.
The commission noted that Aum Shinri Kyo was declared bankrupt last March and nearly all key members were in police custody and undergoing lengthy trials.
The harsh law, promulgated during Japan's labour and leftist turmoil after World War Two, was considered so controversial that it has never been applied to a group.

Aum Shinri Kyo founder Shoko Asahara and dozens of his followers are on trial for murder and other charges for the March 1995 sarin nerve gas attack on Tokyo's subway system, which killed 12 people and made thousands ill.

In criminal court proceedings on Friday, three cult officials -- Masato Yokoyama, Masami Tsuchiya, and Tomomasa Nakagawa -- refused to testify against Asahara in his murder trial for the sarin attack.
Tsuchiya, a cult chemist accused of making the deadly nerve gas, told the Tokyo District Court: "I will not testify because it may have some bearing on my own trial."
He referred to Asahara as master and answered "yes" when asked if he was still an Aum Shinri Kyo believer. All three witnesses bowed towards Asahara before leaving court.
Nearly all of the dozens of other former cult officials have renounced the sect and Asahara.
Asahara, 41, who mumbled incoherently throughout the hearing, was ejected from the court on Thursday for disrupting his murder trial.
